sameOfferedScope.soundUse: If a source claim says a current target is required by a currently offered consumer, actual same-scope context and a full path are necessary; the current Tangens rejection is correct.
sameOfferedScope.falsePositiveRisk: An explicitly reviewed preparatory target can legitimately prepare a later offered stage even when that later consumer is absent from the current entry scope. A universal same-scope rule would reject that distinct semantic claim. Represent it through a separate bounded review contract; do not relax country/scope checks on existing requires-closure.
sameOfferedScope.sufficiencyLimit: Same-scope graph reachability is not sufficient: validate source content and its actual stage. The 7f11 route is the concrete counterexample.
sameOfferedScope.recursiveChainRisk: The wrapper checks one common scope per edge, while the recursive source checker carries no shared scope witness across all registry edges. Add a negative test where A is target in scope1, B context there but target only in scope2, and B->C is source-anchored only in scope2; do not infer a single local witness for A unless a separately reviewed cross-stage preparation contract authorizes it.
